newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong blaze extinguished, death toll at 39.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong blaze extinguished, death toll at 39.

text.p: A blaze in a Hong Kong shop and office block has been extinguished, and 39 people are now confirmed to have been killed in the worst Hong Kong building fire in a century, a senior official said on Thursday.
"This was the most serious (building) fire and the one with the most number of deaths and injuries in the past 100 years," Peter Cheung, director of fire services, told a news conference.
Cheung said the blaze had now been totally extinguished. He said a total of 39 dead had been counted so far. Other officials have said more bodies might still be found.

The fire service mobilised more than 50 fire engines and over 300 staff to battle the blaze, which raged for 20 hours and gutted seven floors of the 16-storey Garley building in the "golden mile" tourist shopping district of Kowloon.

Colonial Governor Chris Patten said earlier that in addition to the deaths, the rescue services were still trying to identify bodies and relate those reported missing to those killed. Many bodies were badly charred and hard to identify, firemen said.
Patten said 78 people had been injured and 39 people had been reported missing. The inferno flared up on Wednesday evening. The cause of the fire is not yet known.
